statement: The first line holds n; the second holds n house values arranged in a circle, so house 0 and house n-1 are neighbours. Rob any set of houses with no two adjacent (around the circle too) and print the maximum haul. The circle breaks the plain pick-or-skip line, and the honest fix is two linear runs: one on houses 0 to n-2, one on houses 1 to n-1 - every valid plan skips the first house or the last, so the better run is the answer. A single house is its own answer.

example.why: Positions 0 and 2 net 1 plus 3; around the circle no better non-adjacent pair exists.

hint: Write the linear robber once as a helper taking a range; call it twice.
mistake: One pass over all n houses - it happily robs both ends, which the circle forbids.
